messages:
Hannah Lee: Quick pulse check on the battlecard deliverables for the ‘Inference at Scale’ webinar. We need concise playbook items: 3 competitor soundbites, routing rules for inbound leads, and two A/B subject lines for follow-up.

Diego Marquez: I'll start with soundbites. Aim for one-liners that call out predictable cost, unified runtime, and rollout flexibility.

Priya Shah: Also add micro-proof points: where we can reference 'dedicated capacity' and 'private deployment' as the direct counters to managed-only messaging.

Noah Patel: Routing rules proposal: if lead mentions any of ["on-prem", "vpc", "compliance"] -> enterprise flow; mentions ["latency", "p99", "slo"] -> infra-specialist; mentions ["cost", "token", "billing"] -> pricing lead. Fallback -> growth SDRs.

Hannah Lee: Love it. Diego, first draft soundbites?

Diego Marquez: Drafts: 
- Cloud AI platforms: "Same ease as hosted APIs, plus predictable economics and routing across hosted/dedicated/private."
- LLM API providers: "Plug-in open models without re-building your serving layer; runtime optimizations do the heavy lifting."
- Infra vendors: "Turnkey serving runtime + orchestration  fewer ops integrations, faster time-to-SLOs."

Priya Shah: Small wording note: avoid jargon like '\u00f7f' (typo?). Also let's add an objection-handling line for 'we already have infra' 
-> "If you already have infra, our runtime can slot in as the serving layer so teams avoid rewrite risk."

Noah Patel: For routing, I drafted a paste-ready rule set for the inbound system (SDRs can copy):
```
{
  "rules": [
    {"keywords": ["on-prem", "vpc", "air-gapped"], "route": "enterprise@redwood.com"},
    {"keywords": ["latency", "p99", "slo"], "route": "infra-specialist@redwood.com"},
    {"keywords": ["cost", "token", "billing"], "route": "pricing@redwood.com"},
    {"keywords": [], "route": "growth-sdr@redwood.com", "fallback": true}
  ]
}
```

Hannah Lee: Nice. For A/B, two subject lines: A) "How much could runtime-aware batching save you?" B) "Can your provider keep 99th-pctl latency during spikes?" We'll measure opens -> demo requests.

Diego Marquez: Competitive rebuttals (short): 
- To 'managed simplicity' claim: "We match simplicity + give you an exit strategy that doesn't require a rewrite."
- To 'full stack provider' claim: "Many vendors promise full stack; we deliver a runtime plus ops primitives so your app stays performant at scale."
- To 'self-hosted is cheaper' claim: "Self-hosted can be cheaper at scale but often hides operational risk and burst costs; our dedicated option gives the economics without surprise invoices."

Priya Shah: I'll assemble the three prioritized rebuttals into bullets for the battlecard and add a recommended opener for SDRs: 'Quick Q: are you optimizing for latency, cost, or compliance?' Add follow-ups per answer.

InboundRouterBot: Lead routed -> route: enterprise@redwood.com, score: 82, matched: ["compliance","vpc"]

Noah Patel: I'll create the Slack alert format: `@enterprise-team new lead {lead_id}: score {score}, kw {keywords}` and drop it in the playbook.

Hannah Lee: Final checklist before I lock the doc: Diego -> finalize soundbites with micro-proofs; Priya -> rebuttal bullets + SDR openers; Noah -> routing JSON + Slack alert; Everyone -> one 8-10 word quote for sales.

Diego Marquez: I'll post final one-liners + micro-proofs by 3pm.

Priya Shah: Rebuttals + SDR opens incoming in 45m.

Noah Patel: Routing and alerts live in the playbook now.

Hannah Lee: Thanks all. I'll synthesize and circulate the final battlecard for sign-off tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
